utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We won't keep you long for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behlo. Mr. Behlo, yesterday I was asking you some questions about a series of orders and I asked you about an order of Enver Zejnilagic which was Exhibit 150, and in that order, in the preamble to that order, it referred to two orders upon which it was based. I took you to the Sefer Halilovic order yesterday evening and then we stopped and I now want to take you to another document that's referred to in that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown Exhibit 152 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I supposed to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, first of all you've got that on the screen now. Yes, could you please just comment on that order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the order. It's in reference to when this operation was supposed to be launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could I just ask you to explain a couple of details of it? First of all, do you have paragraph 2 in front of your eyes there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can the document please be scrolled down? Paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, there it says that one battalion comprising a company of the Prozor Independent Battalion, a company of the 45th Mountain Brigade and two battalions of the 317th Brigade and two platoons of the Sutjeska Battalion shall go on the attack on the Zgon-Brdo-Slime axis. Now could I just ask you to explain to the Court -- sorry, just a moment. Pardon me. Can you just explain to the Court with respect to that map that you drew yesterday, what's the relationship of this order to that map? And I mean the map with the green arrows on it. I think it's 445, the first of the two maps.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order shows precisely the forces and the plan for this operation, the same one that was indicated on the decision that we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When we come to the Halilovic order, which you saw last thing yesterday, dated the 15th of September, what was the need for that Halilovic order, given this -- the existence of this order?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order by Mr. Halilovic is a supplement to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. You explained yesterday to the Judges that if the 6th Corps issued orders to your group or if an officer from the command of the 6th Corps issued orders to your group, you would have to -- or you would seek approval from your own commanders. Now, this order here comes from the 6th Corps but it's directed to you or at least to a battalion of yours in the 317th. So why was it that you, as a member of the 317th Brigade, who is in the 3rd Corps, why was it that you obeyed coming from the 6th Corps and what steps did you have to take before you obeyed it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order by the command of the 6th Corps refers to the operation. There is reference here to considerable forces, about to take part in the operation. They are part of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And who did you personally report to in the course of these combat operations? In other words, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander, Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. Thank you for that. Did you -- yesterday I asked you a couple of questions concerning operations groups and I wish to ask you now a little bit more about that. Could you just explain briefly to the Tribunal, what is an operations group, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: An operations group could be defined as follows. It is made up of several independent units, the levels involved are the battalion level and up. There is a significant amount of both artillery and tanks involved in the composition of an operations group. An operations group is established in order to carry out certain substantial operative assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What sort of order is needed to form an operations group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, an operations group staff must be set up. A commander must be appointed, and it should be determined which units will be part of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you say it should be determined, do you mean that it should be determined by an order, which units should be subordinate to that operations group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What level of -- perhaps when you refer to the staff of an operations group, what sort of branches and components would the staff of an operations group have?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must be -- there must be unit commanders, the commanders of the units involved in the operation, logistics officers, and operatives, operative officers who assist the commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And how does -- in the case where a unit is resubordinated to an operations group, how is such a unit told that they have been resubordinated to an operations group? How is that communicated to them?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an order to set up an operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did any such order ever apply to your battalion in these combat operations in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What was your understanding of the role played by Sefer Halilovic in these combat operations at the time when they were going on?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the Supreme Command Staff. He arrived in the area covered by the 2nd Mountain Battalion with his associates. He stayed in the area for a short time. He probably had assignments that he was supposed to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what was your understanding of -- perhaps I should take a step back from that. You indicated that you had some more substantial contact with Rifat Bilajac. Could you explain the sort of help that Rifat Bilajac gave you on that occasion when you discussed the attack with him?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed Mr. Bilajac the plan or rather the proposed plan for this operation and explained it to him. This was about the operational axes and the deployment of forces. That's what I showed him on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what sort of help did you want from him or need from him?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made several suggestions and provided a number of clarifications. I used these clarifications in order to make a more elaborate plan for the operation, to make a better plan that could more readily be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. And in the end, who did you submit your draft of the plan to?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in touch with Mr. Bilajac, my commander, Mr. Zejnilagic, was there too. He accepted the plan at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did Bilajac issue you with any order whatsoever on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Apart from the order that's in evidence here, the Sefer Halilovic order on the 15th, did you ever see Sefer Halilovic issue an order in the time when he was in that area?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday you indicated that there was an attempt to go into combat on the 16th of September but that you -- your units were surprised by an HVO reconnaissance group and that after that nothing took place. Now, I just want to ask you, were you familiar with the radio station called Radio Rama?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And where was Radio Rama based?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere around the town of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And what do you say about the accuracy of the news that came from Radio Rama in that period? Perhaps let me ask the question another way because that was phrased wrongly. At the time, back in September of 1993, how did you regard the accuracy of Radio Rama back then?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a new radio station that emerged at the time. It was used for propaganda purposes, we believed, the music they played was pretty good but the news was sometimes all wrong and used for mere propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. When you say it was used for propaganda, by whose side was it used for propaganda?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an HVO radio and the propaganda was about spreading information about the situation in our own units and the atmosphere in those towns that were under BH army control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you ever come to hear any rumours or stories that some civilians had been killed in Uzdol during the course of the combat operations on the 14th of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear it at the time, but I did learn later from one of my subordinate officers that there had been problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And can you remember how long after these combat operations -- combat activities you heard that news from one of your subordinates? Was it a matter of days, was it a week, was it more than that? What sort of range of time after?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly several days after the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I just want to turn to some other matters now. Were you interviewed by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor in about 2000 or 2001?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By Mr. Nikolai in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just explain to the junction and the Prosecutor what happened on that occasion? How did the interview proceed and what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was a member of the federal army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the military security service sent me to Sarajevo to the UN headquarters in Sarajevo. I didn't know why I was there or what I'd be doing. Once I reached the building, I was greeted by someone belonging to the investigation team, and they took me to see Mr. Nikolai. I was surprised and very nervous throughout the interview. It was only towards the end of the interview that I found out what the whole thing was about. Mr. Nikolai on that occasion accused me of being a war criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did anything happen with respect to your jacket and your wallet?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the interview first began, I was wearing a leather jacket which I handed to Mr. Nikolai's assistant. They also asked to have my wallet. They took these items away from the interview room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did they say why they wanted those things?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Security reasons, they said. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How did the questioning proceed during that interview?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, I had no idea what that was about. First there were some routine questions, which I answered. Then, Mr. Nikolai told me that he was investigating certain crimes discussed in a book by a Croatian author and he said that my name was dropped too. This book was about war crimes committed against Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When was the name Sefer Halilovic first mentioned during that interview?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps towards the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how were your -- how were your words being recorded during that interview? Was it a taped interview or was there some other mechanism?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was being recorded by Mr. Nikolai on a laptop that he was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, was there anyone else present at any stage during that interview apart from you and Nikolai?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was another gentleman whose name I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, was that gentleman present at all times or part of the time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there most of the time but he would go in and out very often. He would leave the room every now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was doing the typing?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolai.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what language was -- what language were you speaking when you spoke to Mr. Nikolai?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what language was he writing down on -- sorry, what language was he typing into the laptop?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: English, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did he ask you any questions about the role of Sefer Halilovic in an operation called Operation Neretva 93?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he put any propositions to you as to what he thought the role of Halilovic was?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. Leading and we are in an area where it's the witness's testimony which is important, not counsel's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, I understand your question. Maybe you could put your question in another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. How did Mr. Nikolai Mikhailov frame his questions to you concerning Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were imprecise questions, mostly referring to some assessments about which I really couldn't give my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let me put the question straight to you. Did you tell Nikolai Mikhailov that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of this operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not a leading question, if -- my learned friend knows very well that it's not because there is a statement -- well, no. Let me finish and then we'll come to what Mr. Weiner has to say in response. Your Honours, the situation is this, that we have been provided with a document that the Prosecutors have indicated they want to cross-examine this witness on and it's a Nikolai statement. There is a specific part of it that they will want to rely on where the English text says that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, should the witness be removed for this, especially if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Since both parties have that interview, why don't you read those questions and the Court, whatever, in that statement, and ask him to comment, from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honours, but I -- before I do I just want to make the point about these objections. I'm putting the exact proposition that's here to the witness as I'm obliged to do. To object on the basis that it's leading is not proper. The Prosecution know very well what's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, earlier in the Defence case, we give much more leeway to the counsel concerning of the leading questions. But here you could not put to us out of the blue. You have to lay some foundations on that issue. Mr. Weiner, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. Just with regard to cross-examination -- actually examination in direct in this area, what they are trying to do is bolster the credibility of the witness. What they should be doing is: If there is going to be cross-examination on this area, then in redirect examination, then they can enter into the issue. But at this point, they are asking -- they are questioning witnesses as to areas to bolster their credibility, which is not allowable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure it's about the credibility of this witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If the Court looks at the statements you'll see it does concern the credibility of the witness because it concerns prior statements made by the witness which --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's another question. We will let Mr. Morrissey continue and to see how far we could go. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So perhaps if -- Mr. Behlo, there is a statement here in English and I'll ask you about the signatures and so on in just a moment. But I just want to ask you -- the English statement says this, "Enver Zejnilagic told me that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation." My question to you is this: Did you say those words to Nikolai Mikhailov?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Then there is another passage here. And this is in the English statement, it says this: "Enver Zejnilagic introduced me to Sefer Halilovic at the entrance to the school but we did not talk. This was the only one time" - I'm reading from the text there - "this is the only one time that I see Sefer Halilovic during the Operation Neretva-93. It was clear that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation because everybody reported to him." Now, my question to you is: Did you say those words to Nikolai Mikhailov at the time when you made this statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This did not happen and I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could you just explain what the process was after Mr. Nikolai would write words into the computer? At the end of it all, was this statement read back to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nikolai read it back to me before I signed it. However, his assistant took the diskette away to print a copy for signature, and he was reading this statement to me from the laptop, one sentence by one sentence. And then later I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well just to be clear I understand you well, was it read back to you from the laptop or was it read back to you from the paper copy?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the laptop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, could I just show -- just ask that the witness be shown a document now, please. Your Honours, I anticipate the Prosecutor may have an original of this. In any event I'm going to ask that the witness identify this document. So could the witness please be shown this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you identify what the document is so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll get the witness identify what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe you have to inform us about what the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I'm showing the witness a document provided to us by the Prosecution, which is a faxed photocopy with some highlighting on it of Mr. Behlo's name indicating that it's been searched in some way and retrieved in that manner. I'm going to ask him whether his signature is on it but on the face of it it's a statement in the English language taken by Nikolai Mikhailov from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you going to ask the witness to identify the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's the purpose of doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So would you just look at the front page and indicate whether your signature appears there.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And look at the next page and see if you can see your signature there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I notice the court staff are more efficient than I have and have used the ELMO and that's the right thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just point out which one is your signature, thank you. Perhaps just -- could we just look at the first page again and you can identify his signature on the first page as well. Okay, so which one is your signature on the first page?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we go to the third page, please? Can you identify your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, and go to the next page. And does your signature appear on that page?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And does it appear elsewhere on that page as well?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Points]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I just ask you this question? If you knew that that statement contained the two passages that I put to you a little bit earlier, would you have signed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Number one it's a hypothetical question. Number 2, it's very leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, now we have some foundations for this question, and it is a hypothetical question. But in this case, we will allow the Defence to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry about that. So what's the answer? Would you have signed it if you knew that it contained those statements?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was a federal army officer, and automatically we are forbidden to comment on our superior officers. Therefore, at the time I probably could not have said anything like that about an officer who at the time was in the zone of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And after that was all done, what was indicated to you, if anything, about future contacts between yourself and Prosecution investigators, Nikolai in particular?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated that the purpose of the interview was not known to me. I was told that I was mentioned in the book that was the subject of investigation, that my name was mentioned in it. And I was told that for my personal security I should not tell anybody about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You should not tell anybody about what?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I had given a statement and about the procedure in general and that probably they would call me again later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did they call you again later?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did they give you a copy of your statement in Bosnian to read before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I tender that document. I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll hold the admission of this document at a later stage because we have to see whether this is a previous statement or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Or that document might go to the credibility of this witness, as the Prosecution said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it might also go in substantively as a prior inconsistent statement for the testimony that Halilovic was in charge of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If they want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us not go into the substance but at this moment we are not in the position to make a ruling on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if the Prosecutor is seeking to rely on it as a matter of truth, as a matter of the proof of its contents, then there are two things I would say. The first is that this witness wasn't on any list of theirs at any time but secondly I don't want to become embroiled in a discussion about that. What I will do is I'll withdraw the offer for tendering it at this point and we'll consider the matter. The reason why I initially offered it, I make it quite clear, is not to this witness's credibility at all. To someone else. But I withdraw the offer to tender it at this stage and we'll see whether we -- we'll see how cross-examination proceeds before it goes they further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that your decision will not prejudice any offering from the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Should they choose to do so, yes, of course, as the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, since we are in this subject, would you please ask this witness how about his English? Or whether he could understand English?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One of those necessary questions that we forgot about in the excitement. Thank you for reminding me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What languages do you speak?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I speak my mother tongue and, as of recently, I also speak German,

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Those are the questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to assign a number on that document no matter if it's tendered or not since it has been used in this courtroom so that we could identify it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that statement of the witness will be MFI 447.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before counsel sits down, I think you should redact that last statement or portion of it, line 17, 3 for safety of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because in the beginning it was taken in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for that. We will have it redacted. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Philip Weiner and I'm going to ask you some questions on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown that document again? Could we have one on the ELMO? We have copies in English and B/C/S for the Court to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours could it just be indicated when that B/C/S version was produced?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That was just produced yesterday. We have had a copy done. That's not a -- that's produced by our office. That's for the witness to follow, that's all, because we are going to be asking the witness specific questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you produce a B/C/S version of that statement, I believe that you're obliged to furnish it to the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It was given yesterday to the other side. As soon as -- we got it at the break, and they had it right after the break, as soon as we got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that translation checked?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It was done by one of our own certified translators basically just to use in Court and to ask some questions to him. We are not looking to introduce it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us proceed and -- to see how far we could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry, could I just say I would object to the witness being shown a document that has nothing to do with him ever. I don't mind the witness being cross-examined as much as the Prosecution wants from the document that he signed and the matters can be interpreted to him as they go, but to put this version before him now, when he didn't see it and didn't sign it, in my submission, is not permissible. He doesn't need it have it on the ELMO. He can have the relevant portions read to him just as they were, at least in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as the witness testified before, that this witness does not understand English, I believe that this translation is to facilitate the proceedings and we have already made a ruling that we'll let the witness use this document to see how far we could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there is any problem you may raise your objections. Yes. Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Go to page 1, please. Is that your name on the front page, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are my particulars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's your proper date of birth, father's name, place of birth?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's all correct, including your current and former occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's your signature on the bottom of that, sir, isn't that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a typo here at the bottom, in my last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to your statement, today -- let's start off. Yesterday you testified that you didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours could I just intervene there? This is being put that his signature appears on this document. And -- but I understand he's being shown this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The English version. It's clear his signature is on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not disputed it's on the English version. But he's got to be cross-examined, and it's got to be clear. I don't want the record to suggest that he's looking at a document which is signed by him in Bosnian. This is why I objected in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's strictly the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's the English version, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if it's the English version, then it has to be plead clear that's what he's looking at because at the moment, as I understand it, he was given this document. And the role of this document has to be clarified. It has to be clarified which document the witness is looking at, at any given time because later on the record might suggest that he's looking at one when he was looking at the other so it has to be cautious -- when the Prosecutor wants to use two documents, Your Honour allows them I won't say any more about it but they've got to be clear which one it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are referring strictly to the English version. The only need for the Bosnian version is when I read a paragraph so he can follow along. But we are looking strictly at the English version which he signed five times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were asked concerning the function of Mr. Halilovic. I'm sorry, not the function, the powers. And you indicated that you didn't know. When you gave your statement to -- when you gave your statement on March 31st 2001, did you tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the truth then and I'm telling the truth now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you first -- did you tell the truth then is the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's been clearly answered and there is to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he did not answer the question. He started about before and then currently. The question is -- I didn't ask him about what he's speaking today. The question is: Back then, did he tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The answer is "I told the truth then and I'm telling the truth now."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I asked him strictly about then. Move to strike the last portion of the statement. It's not responsive to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. If you want to be more specific, just put your question specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me, was your memory better four years earlier in 2001 as to the events of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that I didn't know what the purpose of the interview was. I spent three and a half years in the war, and I only spent a brief time answering about that period and they were mostly routine questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question was -- the question was simple: Was your memory better four years ago as to the events of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at the next-to-last paragraph in English, on page 2, which in the B/C/S is the first paragraph on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want you to look at the paragraph that begins with the words, "I do not remember for sure when the Operation Neretva started." Do you see that paragraph, sir? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it states there, "I do not remember for sure when the Operation Neretva started. It was in August-September 1993. Enver Zejnilagic told me that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation. My commander Enver Zejnilagic told me that he was the commander of the line of attack on the Voljevac-Crni Vrh-Makljen line." Is that what it says, sir? Did I read that correctly? Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, this witness can't know if he read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have the translations. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I make a suggestion here? I think it's probably the safest way to do it. Mr. Weiner could simply put from the English what he's reading and that can be translated live to the witness and the witness can say that's what he said or that's what he didn't say. To have this document next to him is just going to create confusion. When my friend asks did he read that correctly, well, this witness doesn't speak English and he doesn't know. It's just going to create that sort of difficulty. The questions are legitimate but it's going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that we're doing it right now. I believe whatever the question is, is translated into.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: B/C/S, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he has the copy in front of him to refer and I'll ask him to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us proceed with the interpretations in this courtroom first. If there is any problem, the witness could refer to the translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, in the English on the bottom of that page you've indicated that that's your signature. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to page 3 because I want to ask you just about two or three of these small quotes. Page 3 of the English. The first full paragraph beginning with the words, "Enver Zejnilagic introduced me," which is paragraph 3 on page 3 in the B/C/S version. You see it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "Enver Zejnilagic introduced me to Sefer Halilovic at the entrance to the school but we did not talk. This was the only time that I see Sefer Halilovic during Operation Neretva-93. It was clear that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation because everybody reported to him. The senior military officers then entered the school building where they had a meeting. I was not present at the meeting inside the school." And I'll just continue to the next paragraph. "After the meeting, Enver Zejnilagic and I went back to Voljevac, and while in the car, Enver Zejnilagic told me that Sefer Halilovic agreed to and approved our suggestion to attack in the direction of Voljevac, Crni Vrh, Makljen." Is that -- did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that again. It's got -- it is irrelevant in this case whether Mr. Weiner read it correctly. It's just -- relates to the confusion that's caused by using these two documents. It's not important whether he read it correctly. There is an obvious purpose the Prosecutor is allowed to achieve but -- there is another objection coming, but we'll wait until they actually put the question. But with respect to that, I object to that question and it's really juggling the two documents, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. Weiner is laying down the foundation --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- at this stage, which he's allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And on the bottom of that page in the English, page 3, again, is your signature?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the answer isn't indicated. When I read those two paragraphs, did I read those correctly, sir? My previous question, those two paragraphs that I read, did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to persist with this objection. He doesn't matter whether he read them correctly or not. It's not important. The issue is: Does the witness agree that his signature appears on the bottom of the page. What Mr. Weiner didn't do with the last one and what he hasn't done here is to put to him, is that true? Is that what you said? That's what's being avoided here by this device, and in my submission this line of questioning is I don't want to cast aspersions of ill faith but it's dancing around the issue of whether he read things correctly or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Some people like to do it step by step. I believe the next step will be the question you suggested. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, sir, did I read those two paragraphs correctly or would you like me to read them again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, my learned friend ought to establish the expertise of the witness to indicate how he can give an opinion whether Mr. Weiner is reading correctly or not. He cannot offer an opinion on that topic. Now, it's a technical objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have the interpretations and we have the B/C/S versions at this stage. I believe that the witness is in the position to answer this question. There is no need for the expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope you should not interrupt so often on the cross-examination. You may proceed, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, again did I read those two paragraphs correctly or would you like me to read them again?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I had signed the English statement. At that point in time, I wasn't aware of its meaning, and now I see that it was written accurately and I think you're reading what it says was accurate too. Most of the time I explained about those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, didn't you state on two occasions, in 2001, to the interpreter and the investigator in that room that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of that operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, there is some problem with your question because from the transcript we could see that the witness was told. It's not his personal knowledge. He was told, you have to put it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you tell the investigator and the interpreter in 2001 that you were told by Enver Zejnilagic that Sefer Halilovic was in charge and that it was clear to you that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation because everyone reported to him?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember providing that specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you're not saying you did not do it? You don't recall at this time; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave an answer at the time to the question asked, but I don't remember giving this very answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you turn to page 4 in the English for a moment? On the top of the page it is in Bosnian, the Bosnian language. Do you see at the top of that page it says in Bosnian, "Witness acknowledgement"?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it says -- why don't you read what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "This statement was read out loud to me in the Bosnian language. It accurately reflects what I said to the best of my memory. I gave this statement of my own free will and am aware that it may be used in proceedings before the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia for war crimes committed since 1991. I am also aware that I may be summoned to testify before the Tribunal."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, is that your signature right below your acknowledgement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I wrote the date myself, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you knew at that time that you might be called to testify before the Tribunal, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also knew at that time that this statement could be used in legal proceedings before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you also indicate there the first sentence or the first -- in the first sentence that this statement has been read over to me in the Bosnian language. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we continue below that, if we look in the English and the Bosnian, there is something known as an interpreter's certification. Do you see that? Do you see that in the statement, sir? On page 4 of the English version, and it's also in the B/C/S at the end, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in that interpreter's certification your name appears in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it says, "I have been informed by Mehmed Behlo that he speaks and understands the Bosnian language." In paragraph 3, it says, "I have orally translated the above statement from English -- from the English language to the Bosnian language in the presence of Mehmed Behlo who appeared to have heard and understood my translation of this statement." Paragraph 4, "Mehmed Behlo has acknowledged that the facts and matters set out in this statement as translated by me are true to the best of his knowledge and recollection and has accordingly signed his signature where indicated." Then there is a signature below that. And isn't your signature below that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not state that someone else read that statement to you. Rather, he said that he read that statement to you. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, is this necessary to ask this question to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think everything is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It -- if the Court gives me some leave we will see why. We have a 92 bis statement from the interpreter indicating that he in fact read the statement and that he read every word of that statement to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, you can see why there might be an objection on a number of bases to that comment made at this time. But at this stage in any event we are dealing with a witness who is in court. If the Prosecutor wants to ask questions of this witness then he can. And I don't object to that. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, you read everything in paragraph by paragraph already into the transcript, and the witness agreed that he signed this document already. So do we have to go into the very details?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll just ask him one follow-up question and move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know of any reason why the interpreter would have stated that he read the full statement to you if it wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. We don't know what the situation is with that interpreter, and this witness shouldn't be asked to speculate about that witness's motives, contacts with Nikolai or any other matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's not speculation, Your Honour. He can see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, I believe you have exhausted all the questions on that issue. The situation is very clear, at least in our mind. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's move on. I'm going to ask you some related questions to this and then take you back to the statement. You testified that you were a member of the 317th motorised Brigade, isn't that correct.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was part of the Zapad OG, operations group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of Zapad operations group, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cikotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, your commander, Enver Zejnilagic reported to Selmo Cikotic, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that Selmo Cikotic has testified in this case, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you aware, on 23 February 2005, on pages 17 and 18, Selmo Cikotic testified that Sefer Halilovic led and coordinated this operation and was issuing orders to units tasked by this operation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. I don't think the witness is aware of the testimony. You may say that the witness -- another witness said as follows. Do you agree with him or not? Is that true, or along this line, but you could not ask whether the witness was aware of that testimony or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In the details, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, was the commander of your operational group, Selmo Cikotic, in a better position than you to know the position of -- and role of Sefer Halilovic during Operation Neretva?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was Commander Cikotic in a better position than you to know of Halilovic's position and role in the operation in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was in a better position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the reason I asked the last question is because, Your Honour, I would ask him this next question. And, sir, must you not admit that Selmo Cikotic's testimony is practically the same as your statement on page 2 and 3, basically, that Sefer Halilovic was in charge of the operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, we could compare the testimony by ourselves. There is no need for the witness to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified about receiving orders from the 6th Corps. Were you present during -- were you present during meetings between Sefer Halilovic and Salko Gusic, the 6th Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On just one occasion, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That was in Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you present during any other meetings between Salko Gusic, the commander of the 6th Corps, and Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you present during any conversations between the commander of the 6th Corps, Salko Gusic, and Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know what orders in relation to Operation Neretva Sefer Halilovic gave Salko Gusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not right to put that question in that form because the witness hasn't agreed that Mr. Halilovic gave any orders to Salko Gusic whereas that question presumes that he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know what if any orders in relation to operation Neretva that Salko Gusic -- I'm sorry, that Sefer Halilovic gave to Salko Gusic, the commander of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, I attended this one meeting. Most of all it was logistical matters that were discussed. General Halilovic was there, as well as the 6th Corps commander, Salko Gusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question was, sir, do you know what if any orders in relation to Operation Neretva Sefer Halilovic gave to Salko Gusic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know of none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I'll ask you this question, sir: Was your commander, Selmo Cikotic, in a better position than you to hear and observe Halilovic giving orders to the commander Salko Gusic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That strikes me as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that during the interviewing session, there was an interpreter that was present. You were aware that Nikolai Mikhailov was an investigator?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the interpreter was a freelancer hired by the Registry of this Tribunal to interpret?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the interpreter was not an employee of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that on Friday evening or early evening, or -- in The Hague, that the interpreter has provided what we call a 92 bis statement in relation to your interview? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that within that statement, the interpreter has stated, the words in the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop here, please. I object, and I do not wish this to be on the record. Your Honours, we've got significant objections to make to this procedure that the Prosecution seem to be flirting with, but they should not be permitted to put on the record in the form of a question to this witness the contents of any alleged such document. It's not a proper matter to cross-examine the witness on, now that the answer has been given that the witness was not even aware of the taking of such a statement, if you look at the previous answer. So Your Honours we object to this question being put or any questions being put arising out of a document that the Prosecutors may have in their possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was provided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- to the Defence on the weekends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage we are not familiar with any 92 bis statements in relation to your interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. I object to that being tendered. Now, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe, Mr. Weiner, before you furnish this to us, could you please tell us what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a 92 bis statement which was signed by a presiding officer, a Mr. Haider, at about 6.00 on Friday evening. It is a statement of Mark Jeffery pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Mark Jeffery is an interpreter. Mark Jeffery went on that mission and interpreted several statements. He is going to state that the witness -- that he personally read every word, every line, every phrase, of each of those statements, that he read them in Bosnian. What they would do is there would be an interview, it would be typed by Mr. Nikolic [sic] he would then sit at the computer, fix the spacing and grammar and go over line by line with the witness every word, every phrase. Then they would print it out. Then he would go through the corrected statement because there would be numerous corrections. The corrected statement with the witness, he would then have the witness sign it. He would then have the witness sign the witness attestation. He would then sign a certificate indicating that he read this statement to the person and he would have the witness co-sign it. And that's what he did with Mr. Behlo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, we have that previous document. On the page 4 there is an interpreter certification. So you don't think that is enough? You don't think that is reliable so you also provide that 92 bis statement last Friday? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- it goes -- it does not go to the acts and conduct of the defendant and as a result we got this based on the notes that we received from the Defence that there was going to be in our view changes as to the previous statement. We basically went out and got a statement from Mr. Jeffery that the interviews were taken above board, that there was nothing that -- that there was nothing below board or that there was no subterfuge in these interviews. Now, Defence has made allegation after allegation against the investigator. We have a witness, an independent witness, and unless they are going to say that there was this conspiracy between a freelance interpreter and the investigator, we have an independent witness here saying that this was an above-board interview and he made those statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm very, very reluctant to go into a kind of voir dire procedures on that issue, if it's not essential to your case, Mr. Weiner. I wonder whether it's necessary to have this 92 bis statement. And we have the different procedure for the admission of 92 bis statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, could you please indicate to me how long your cross-examination will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, if I have an idea if the statement is going to be able to be used, I'll have a better idea. It shouldn't be lasting more than another half hour, 45 minutes, but if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. What do you want me to respond to, the suggestion to use that statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, there is a number of objections to using such a statement. The Defence has been very critical of Nikolai Mikhailov and we continue to be. I make it quite clear. Now, if the Prosecution has a desire to impugn this witness, well, then, they may seek in the normal course of events to do that in their rebuttal case. If that's what they wish -- really wish to do. We understand the Prosecutor would be concerned about the attestation on that statement and why they might wish to bolster it and prop it up. Of course, if that happens, they should go through the proper procedures. We don't mind the Prosecutor testing this witness on the substance of -- or put the propositions to the witness, you know, wasn't he told everything, didn't he really say this, just the normal cross-examination that happens. To use this document here is just impermissible, it's not a 92 bis situation. Their case is closed. If they want to lead evidence, they can seek to do it in rebuttal. Meanwhile, they should put the questions that they have to put. This 92 bis in my submission was just a plainly an attempt to get this on to the record now and Your Honour should not permit that document to be used in evidence at this stage. The Prosecution can make the proper application at the proper time, and with the proper notice. And with the Defence being allowed to make inquiries about this individual and exactly what his relationship was with Nikolai Mikhailov and so on. My learned friend says he's independent but we don't know anything about him and we are not prepared to accept anything from the bar table about this person. So we've received this very late. We don't know anything about Mr. Jeffery. Your Honour, the Prosecutor can adequately do his job by putting the questions and the propositions to this witness that he wants to put, and that's what I submit is the right course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultation with my colleagues, I believe that this Bench is in a position to make a ruling, that this 92 bis statement is not allowed to use. However, the Prosecution is free to file a motion on the admission of this 92 bis statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were just going to use this, not to introduce, but to use it to impeach him or actually question him between -- with relation to the conflict and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You could ask direct questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In relation to what's in this statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, of course it's in relation to the statement but, however, but however, you could not use this statement. I believe that it's time for us to take a break. We'll take a very short break and we'll -- that is about 20 minutes. We'll resume at 10 minutes to 11. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will sit for an hour. Then we will have our next break. We will try to finish the testimony of this witness within an hour. If not, we'll have another break. Mr. Weiner, I believe that you have made your point crystal clear on this issue, and we are all professional judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm moving on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: All the judges are permanent Judges of this Tribunal. So I hope you could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm moving on. Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday about an order to attack signed by Enver Zejnilagic, and you stated that you had drafted this document with Commander Zejnilagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 150, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is it on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we move to paragraph number 10, which is on the second page in the B/C/S, and the third page in the English? Do you see that paragraph, sir? Could you read it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you read it to yourself and familiarise yourself with that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when it says, "Security support," does that concern the role or the task of the military police or the military security unit?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the task relating to the security of all the units, unit commands and communication units participating in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was the military security or the military police, was it their duty or task to carry that out?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was first something that had to be done by the units mentioned in the order, and then there is also a task here for the police that was to protect the command post and the communication centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the last sentence says, "I most strictly prohibit looting, slaughtering and killing of innocent civilians, while prisoners of war shall be treated according to the regulations on prisoners of war." Was that -- did that concern all units or just the military police? Or both?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerns all units participating in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was the military security, were they responsible, or military police, as part of this, and as part of that, and pursuant to that prohibition that I just read, were they to ensure that prisoners of war were not -- that were captured were not harmed? Or mistreated?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This had to be done by the units out in the field and not by the police. That was the general principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And had you ever seen a similar paragraph in any order or a similar prohibition, I most strictly prohibit looting, slaughtering and killing of innocent civilians, while prisoners of war shall be treated according to the regulations and prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this also refers to an order by the 6th Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you have to put that type of strict order in there to ensure that civilians are not murdered or their property isn't looted, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all operations, the main and the key order is the order relating to the operation or the order to attack or order to defend, just as it is reflected in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you know, sir, that in all wars, that civilians have been harmed and injured and their property has been looted, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always set out from our own situation, and our situation was that it was our task to protect our civilians and our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as a result, you have to put it in -- you have to tell the troops orally and in writing, as you did it here, that civilians should not be harmed or killed or their property should not be looted, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers must be familiar with the order to the extent that they are required to be familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as a preventive measure in this document, you placed the words, "I most strictly prohibit looting, slaughtering, and killing of innocent civilians," you placed these words there as a preventive measure to make sure the soldiers didn't do that, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a security measure relating to security, just like you have logistics, intelligence, attacks from the air. These are measures of safety or security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct. And to prevent any harm to civilians, you placed that statement in there as a security measure?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This primarily referred to, for example, if we carried out the task, and continued fighting in inhabited places.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that the Geneva Conventions does not permit the murder of civilians?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We always knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it doesn't permit the looting of civilian property?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it does not permit the mistreatment of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in the words of this statement, you -- it says, "I most strictly prohibit, looting, slaughtering and killing of innocent civilians," to prevent such action from occurring?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a security measure to prevent something like that from happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, moving on to another topic, sir, you told us that your command post for your 2nd Battalion was in Voljevac, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And now the Prozor Independent Battalion was to your left, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that there was a command post of the Prozor Independent Battalion in Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of their command posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One of their command posts. And what was the distance between Voljevac where your command post was, and Dobro Polje, where one of the command posts of the Prozor Independent Battalion was located?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that your area of responsibility went to the village of Here, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not my area of responsibility. That was where the boundaries met of my area of responsibility and the independent battalion's area of responsibility, the village of Here was within the Prozor Independent Battalion area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct. My question wasn't as specific. Your area of responsibility went up to the village of Here, to the border of the village of Here, correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Here overlooks Uzdol, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uzdol is located below the villages of Here, Scipe and Kute.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what was the distance from your border at the beginning of Here to Uzdol, in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to ten kilometres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you knew that Enver Buza was the commander of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And since that battalion was on your left flank or just to your left, you had to have communicated with that battalion. There had to be communication between the two units.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with any of the soldiers that were members of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall any of the soldiers right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Since you were only 22 years old at the time, did you go to school or attend school with any members of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't. They attended school in Prozor and I went to school in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, were you aware that a number of the members of the Prozor Independent Battalion had been imprisoned by the Croats and used as human shields before they were released and became members?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And those persons who were used as human shields, from what area did they come from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly Bosniaks from the area of the Prozor municipality, and other areas occupied by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Uzdol was part of the Prozor municipality, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was occupied by the HVO at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were aware, on September 14th, that the Prozor Independent Battalion was involved in combat in the village of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were not aware that combat occurred in Uzdol on that date?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew that there was fighting but I didn't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you have contact that day with the Prozor Independent Battalion, since they were on your flank, they were right next to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So they were involved in fighting on your flank but you didn't know what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were reporting to their superior command, whereas I and my men concentrated on our own task.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
