utterances.text: But where they were on your flank, if something happened to them, it could quickly affect your troops. So were you monitoring their actions or were you in any communication with them as to what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there is a sentence and then there is a question. And the witness had better be asked whether he agrees with the first sentence before he goes on to the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness could answer that question in one answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As long as he understands he's got the chance to answer that first one but the sentence that's there as well as the question that follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no need. I remember the question. In my area of responsibility, and along the axes of attack, there were about a thousand soldiers deployed, and we were just working to organise the soldiers for the tasks. On the other side, there was a small number of soldiers who were in the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the question is: Were you aware of what they were doing? That's all. Did you monitor their activities on that date?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard some kind of infantry combat, and we expected them to join the combat because it was a joint front. But we didn't know specifically what exactly it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you heard that over the military radio system?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was something that was conveyed to me by my commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the commanders were in radio contact and were coordinating operations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My commanders were close to the area of responsibility of the Prozor Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So they were monitoring what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were monitoring what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you or Commander Zejnilagic learn on September 14th that some people had been killed in Uzdol, be it soldiers, civilians, be it ABiH soldiers, but anyone had been killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had some information that indicated that soldiers of the Prozor Independent Battalion suffered a failure, that they had a lot of casualties, that they had entered a minefield somewhere on the border of the area of responsibility of our two battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And within a few days, you said you heard on Radio Rama that some -- or someone had told you they heard on Radio Rama that civilians had been killed in Uzdol, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that from my security officer, who heard that from an officer who was operating the communication lines. I think that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that Radio Rama played good music or some nice music. Did a lot of the soldiers listen to Radio Rama?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a shortage of batteries for radios at that time but the radio was listened to in some places, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did other soldiers hear that same news flash, that civilians had been killed in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anybody comment on that. There were probably some soldiers who had heard it, but I don't know exactly who that was or how many soldiers had heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what they were describing on Radio Rama wasn't the killing of a -- one or two civilians. They were describing the killing of a number of civilians. Did they use the word "massacre" or the killing of the whole village? What do you recall? They were -- what do you recall, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not hear Radio Rama at the time, but I heard a version of the events from one of my officers, just briefly that there was mention of something like that happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you notify your commander up the line as to what you'd been told about civilians being killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just one clarification in the transcript, sir. You said something -- there was mention of something like that happening. When you say something like that, was that in relation to the statement I -- or the word I used of a massacre occurring?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the news item on Radio Rama. Something like what Radio Rama was talking about, but I don't know what exactly they said, just by habit we knew that they had their own version of some events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But, sir, did you contact anyone in the Prozor Independent Battalion when you'd heard that there was a problem in Uzdol right over your border, that something had happened there, civilians were killed? Did you ask anyone, speak to anyone about that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to your commanders who were monitoring the situation in Uzdol if they had observed anything or if they had heard anything?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did talk to my superior officers, but we simply concluded that the Prozor Independent Battalion was facing problems in their own area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they had to come to grips with these problems. If any assistance was needed, we would only be too glad to provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: First, how many officers did you speak to concerning what you had heard?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I remember is that I spoke to my security officer, who was a physician by profession. We analysed a number of situations and we talked about a number of different things, important things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said -- you just said that you had -- "I did talk to my superior officers" in relation to the question of who did you speak to. Which of your superior officers did you speak to about the situation in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My security officer and I had also the company commanders. One of them, the nearest, in the village of Here because that was his area of responsibility, would regularly inform me about any relevant situation that occurred. However, the reports I would receive from him were superficial, so we didn't pay it much heed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Since the village of Uzdol was just over your border, did you speak to anyone about this situation, anyone else, about this situation that had occurred, where a number of civilians were killed, to try and find out what happened?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back then, we were facing a great deal of difficulty, trying to consolidate our units. We did a great deal of work trying to improve the situation in our unit, in view of the fact that we had suffered a failure in our previous operations. At that point in time, what mattered most were the problems we were facing in terms of organisation and logistics. We simply didn't have enough time to deal with the rest. We were only interested in what lay within our area of responsibility. Back then, no operations were under way and we believed we would have enough time to come to grips with these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you just give me the names of those persons that you spoke to? You mentioned one who was a doctor. You said your security officer. What were the names of the persons you spoke to? You mentioned a commander.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security officer, Senad Masetic a physician by profession, he was, and he still is. The other person was Sead Suptic, company commander. His area of responsibility was in the village of Prdvortci [phoen], which neighboured on the area covered by the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that it? Is that all you can think of right now?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the two persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did anyone from military police or military security ever question you about Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the military police or military security ever question any members of your battalion about Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of. May be the case, it's just that I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from the military police or military security ever question anyone in the 317th Brigade concerning the deaths in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was any -- was there any request that -- was there any request or order for you to place in writing a report about the activities of your units or the lack of activity of your units in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did anyone even question if your units or the units of the 317th participated in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, Nikolai asked me such a question the first time around.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you answered that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In 2001, in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I -- moving on to one other matter, you testified about operational groups today. Do you have any experience or back in 1993 did you have any experience in relation to operational groups formed at Supreme Command level?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in any way at the time. Nor was I familiar with any operations groups with the exception of OG West. Later on, at the final stage of the war, I was involved in a number of operations with my own units which were part of certain operations groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, sir, since you weren't familiar with operations groups formed at the Supreme Command level, you're not aware whether Sefer Halilovic was in command of an operational group leading Neretva 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to that. It misstates what the witness's previous evidence was and it contains factual difficulties and that question is not permissible on a number of bases, but if Your Honour looks here it says, "since you were not familiar with operations groups formed at the Supreme Command level," that question hasn't been asked of him yet. He simply asked whether he knows what an operations group is. I won't repeat what I asked him and what the evidence was but Your Honours have heard it all and the Prosecutor has to ask the questions before putting the proposition to him and go step by step, in my submission, before butting a multi-layered question like that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness answered that he was not familiar with any operations group with the exception of the OG West. So he is only familiar with the operational group of the OG West, which implies that he does not familiar with any operational group formed by the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I concede. I agree, that's correct. I think my learned friend's question concerned expertise and ability to comment on that but perhaps I'm wrong about it. Anyway, we will see what the witness says. Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you like me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not familiar with any unit of that kind back then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So therefore you weren't familiar or you didn't know whether Sefer Halilovic was in command of one leading Operation Neretva?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew at the time, he was not the commander of any operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you weren't familiar with any operational groups at the Supreme Command level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's an argument that's being put, not a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I believe that the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At this point, I would like to tender his statement, Your Honour, which the Defence initially tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honour. The Prosecutor hasn't sought to lay a basis for doing that yet or said why it is that he wanted to do it. It's a matter that we can argue now. If my friend has finished his cross-examination. I've got very brief re-examination. Otherwise we can deal with it at the end. Or I'll deal with it now if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as a normal practice, as you know, that we do not admit the previous statement of the witness since we have this witness testified live in this Tribunal. And during the cross-examination, we believe that most of these central issues have been touched upon so there is no need to admit the previous statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, there is -- there's two small segments of re-examination and could I just indicate I've just got a short number of questions arising out of the, if you like, facts matters and then I just wanted to look at some transcript. My learned friend put some material from the evidence of a previous witness and I just wanted to check a transcript about that before I finish which I think I need three minutes to do, Your Honour. I've tried to do it in the running but I had to listen to my learned friend. Anyway I'll ask the simple questions now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behlo. You were asked questions by the Prosecutors about where did you get your information concerning the problems -- sorry, the combat in Uzdol. And you said to the Prosecutors that you got this information from your commanders and I think you used the word "komandiri." Now, does that word, "komandiri," does that mean junior commanders or your superior commanders, in other words the commanders under you at the company level and so on or over you at the superior level?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. It's leading, why don't you just ask him what it means instead of giving him hints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. What's the meaning of the term komandiri? Does that mean superior or inferior commanders or does it mean something different altogether?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word komandiri refers to junior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you said to the Prosecutor that you received news about combat operations from komandiri in the Uzdol -- near to Uzdol, can you remember who those komandiri were of yours?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, the commander of the 2nd Company. The area of responsibility of his unit neighboured on that of the 2nd Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just to clarify these matters, did you receive any information about that Uzdol combat from any superior commanders of yours?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were asked questions by the learned Prosecutor about whether you spoke to anyone at the Prozor Independent Battalion after you heard the story about the Radio Rama broadcast. And I just want to ask you this: At that time, how good or bad were your relations with the commander, Enver Buza?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED BEHLO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regrettably, it was necessary for us to have good relations. However, from the outset, they were never what they were meant or supposed to be. That is to say they weren't good. That precisely was the reason why I allowed my logistics officer to deal with some of the responsibilities and I also delegated some of those to my company commander because they were in close contact with the Prozor Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honours permit me now a very short recess just to check these things? As I indicated, I would only need two or three minutes. I know what I would be interested in but events moved a little quicker than I thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, less than three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. There is no need to adjourn the Court. I don't seek that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not going to ask any further questions based on this. I wish to point something out to Your Honours but it needn't concern the witness. That's the redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this stage, are there any documents to tender by the parties? It seems to me there are none. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the courtroom. We wish you a very pleasant journey back home. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage we are not sure whether we could hear the next witness or not tomorrow. Maybe the Defence could inform us this afternoon so that we could arrange the hearings for tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's a medical report we are awaiting the details. We will advise as we have them. We -- our current schedule is we should know, we hope to know by 1.00 today and we'll tell the Prosecutors and the Chamber straight away, of course. There was going to be another witness scheduled for this week. He's been withdrawn. Your Honours, could I just -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes. Look, my learned friend asked some questions of the witness based on the testimony of Commander Cikotic who was the commander of the Operations Group Zapad. Your Honour, it's the fact that I put transcript to witnesses from time to time and as a matter of principle I don't oppose the Prosecutor doing it in an appropriate case. But when it relates to expert type of evidence or technical type of comment, it raises a problem, and I was tempted with the idea of putting slabs of Cikotic's evidence to this witness. In the end what I thought would be the best thing to do is just simply to remind the Chamber of -- that Cikotic gave a great deal of evidence. It's dated the 23rd of February of this year. And there are parts in it on which the Prosecutor relies and parts on which we rely and we would ask the Chamber consider that evidence in its entirety benefitting the Prosecutor and benefiting the Defence and just to read it in its entirety. Because this witness's comments about that evidence are unlikely to help. It would be different if they said something different about an event that took place and of course then it's appropriate to do it. And I obviously don't oppose that being done. As it is, because the Prosecutors raised the Cikotic material, I would ask, although it may seem like an onerous thing to ask, that the Chamber consider reading the evidence of Cikotic, the transcript of that. I know that will be done at the end, because it's been raised with there witness and one part was put to him, it leaves us in the position of either reading large slabs out or just relying on the Chamber to read what -- what you've noted as being of significance there. And so we do ask that that evidence be taken as a whole at all times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe this is our practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Your Honours, my lack of experience as a judge means that I have to be anxious and cautious at all times. Of course, we understand that -- that Your Honours will do that and I say it perhaps to make sure that I'm not conceding that part of Cikotic's evidence that was put is to be taken in isolation as it was. That's really all I wanted to say about it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for reminding me of that. Well, I believe that's all for today's hearing. If there is nothing that the parties would like to raise, the hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.45 a.m.,
